rv.q: It's genuinely inspiring without resorting to preaching or sentimentality and I warrant you'll leave feeling at least a little bit better about the world.
This is feel-good theater, the kind that bathes you generously in sincere appreciation for simple acts of friendship.
Above all, Smallwood’s performance as Kenneth is a real testament to his superb abilities as a performer and the intimacy of PRIMARY TRUST becomes more profoundly emotional thanks to him.
The Goodman ’s Chicago-premiere production of Primary Trust by Eboni Booth is everything I’ve been craving in theatre lately.
This recent Pulitzer Prize-winning play is a true winner.
There is not one false step in Primary Trust.

In the delicate hands of director Malkia Stampley, this is a fine production of a rare play whose great wisdom and humanity unfolds slowly and curiously, like epiphanies that spring up from a lifetime.
The production offers a quiet yet profound reflection on human connection, personal growth, courage, and the essential need for primary trust.
Eboni Booth's Primary Trust is a love story about the mind and how tragic circumstances can sequester us from humanity but never touch the beauty of our soul to love, live, and survive.
A play of unvarnished eloquence, Eboni Booth’s poignant, uplifting portrait of a solitary, emotionally wounded man navigating a major life change received 2024’s Pulitzer Prize for drama.
Booth's play is expertly cast and directed by Malkia Stampley in what marks her impressive Goodman directing debut.

In a compact ninety minutes, Booth takes the audience on a compelling journey, one with much to say about human connection, and it’s not surprising to me that this exceptional work was the recipient of a Pulitzer Prize for Drama.
This was 90 minutes of high quality story-telling that brought us a great story about friendship, love, adjustment and work ethics.

cn.t: Critics praise Eboni Booth's Pulitzer Prize-winning play as a deeply moving, warmhearted exploration of loneliness and human connection, elevated by Namir Smallwood's soulful, beautifully realized central performance as Kenneth.
